content:
@Kevin Buzzard noticed in a comment on #39155 that shake --fix was adding unnecessary imports of import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.Elementwise to 

- Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Colimits
- Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Limits

and this was causing the elementwise attribute to panic.

I had Claude take a look and attempt a minimization and after reviewing this, here's my best understanding of what's going on.

First, elementwise is used in both ConcreteCategory/Elementwise.lean and Limits/Types/{Limits,Colimits}.lean and the same declarations end up generated in different parts of the import tree (for example limit.lift_π_apply and limit.w_apply are generated by both ConcreteCategory/Elementwise.lean and Limits/Types/Limits.lean). Currently, the only file that imports ConcreteCategory/Elementwise.lean and Limits/Types/Limits.lean is the top-level Mathlib.lean.

When shake --fix was run, when looking at Limits/Types/Limits.lean the explain output said:

  note: `import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.Elementwise` required
    because `CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Limit.w_apply` refers to `CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.w_apply`

Here shake resolved limit.w_apply to the copy in ConcreteCategory.Elementwise rather than the one generated in Limits/Types/Limits.lean itself. (There is a simpler minimization of this in the repro repo (same as the one linked above)).

With the new import, elementwisein Limits/Types/Limits.lean now panics when it tries to create limit.w_apply because it calls addRelatedDecl which apparently does not handle well the case when a name already exists in an imported module.

It seems to me like there are multiple steps where we could / should fix things here, but I've never looked at this code before so I'd like to hear other opinions.

cc: @Anne Baanen @Dagur Asgeirsson @Sebastian Ullrich @Thomas Murrills

It definitely seems like addRelatedDecl should at least handle the existing-constant case more gracefully, possibly with a flag to allow the calling metaprogram to determine its erroring behavior (to distinguish this kind of "maybe-acceptable" failure from other ones).

Bryan Gin-ge Chen said:

the same declarations end up generated in different parts of the import tree (for example limit.lift_π_apply and limit.w_apply are generated by both ConcreteCategory/Elementwise.lean and Limits/Types/Limits.lean).

More generally I'm wondering if this pattern is a good one given that these aren't reserved names? :thinking: My first instinct is that not reserving the names makes it a bit of an abuse of this property of importing theorems, but I'm not sure if there's precedent for it.
Duplicated theorems definitely sounds troublesome, I don't even want to guarantee future Lean versions supporting that

That makes sense; I figured this might be more something that should be fixed on the mathlib side. However, should I open an issue suggesting that shake throws an error or warning in a case like this?
I don't think it's that easily detectable
I think that from the duplicated attributes, one of the two should be removed, and then shake should be attempted again after that.

I'm probably misunderstanding your message but since ConcreteCategory.Elementwise doesn't currently import Limits.Types.{Colimits,Limits} (and vice versa), removing the attributes in one of the files might break something, right? (I haven't tried yet).
Yes, we might have to change the imports

I finally got back to this and have opened:

  • #41422 which fixes the panic in addRelatedDecl
  • #41425 which adjusts the imports so that elementwise is no longer generating the same declarations twice.

Unless I'm missing something, these both should be fairly straightforward.
